description: Fishermen were allowed less than a third of the area allocated under Oslo - six of 20 nautical miles. As of July 2014 Israel limited fishing to three nautical miles, barring access to the more fertile grounds. Oxfam notes the reduction from six to three prevented access to 85% of the waters agreed at Oslo.
energy_note: Eighty-five per cent of the sea, closed.

aspect: The fish are not in the permitted water
description: The sardine and larger pelagic grounds are further out. The permitted strip is over-fished, shallow and depleted, so effort rises while the catch falls.
money_note: Annual income difference for a fishing household.
energy_note: Fishing all day in the part with no fish.

aspect: Crossing the line is shot at
description: The limit is enforced by naval fire, arrest and boat confiscation. A navigational error is not a fine.
money_note: Value of a confiscated boat and gear.
energy_note: A wrong turn at sea is live fire.

aspect: It removes the cheapest protein from a food-insecure population
description: 57% of Gaza households were food insecure and about 80% were aid recipients. Restricting the fishery removes the one locally produced protein source that does not need a crossing permit.
energy_note: The one food nobody has to import, restricted.

description: The Oslo Accords allocated 20 nautical miles. Fishermen were permitted six, and as of July 2014 Israel limited fishing to three - barring access to the more fertile grounds and, per Oxfam, preventing access to 85% of the waters agreed.
energy_note: Twenty miles on paper, three in the water.
